name: Replace untrusted unserialize and assess the chain
query: A security report says our wishlist cookie handling allows PHP object injection. Fix it.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Run wordpress-router to classify repo kind
Step 2: Run wp-project-triage to detect plugin structure
Step 5: Identify unserialize()/maybe_unserialize() on cookie data as PHP object injection
Step 6: Replace serialize/unserialize with wp_json_encode()/json_decode() and validate the decoded structure
Step 7: Search the plugin for magic methods (__wakeup, __destruct, __toString) with side effects and explain how they could chain with the injection
Step 8: Remove those side effects, or make the class refuse unserialization
Step 9: Search for other unserialize()/maybe_unserialize() calls on untrusted data
success_criteria: No unserialize()/maybe_unserialize() on cookie or request data remains
Decoded wishlist data is validated (expected types, allowed keys)
Magic methods with dangerous side effects are found and fixed, not only the reported line
The response describes the chained impact, not only the single finding
